In [[probability theory]], the ''' Vysochanskij–[[Yuri Petunin|Petunin]] inequality ''' gives a lower bound for the [[probability]] that a [[random variable]] with finite [[variance]] lies within a certain number of [[standard deviation]]s of the variable's [[expected value|mean]], or equivalently an upper bound for the probability that it lies further away. The sole restrictions on the [[probability distribution|distribution]] are that it be [[unimodal function|unimodal]] and have finite [[variance]]; here ''unimodal'' implies that it is a continuous probability distribution except at the [[mode (statistics)|mode]], which may have a non-zero probability.

== Theorem ==

Let <math>X</math> be a random variable with unimodal distribution and finite variance, and <math>\alpha\in \mathbb R</math>. If we define <math>\rho=\sqrt{\mathbb E[(X-\alpha)^2]}</math> then for any <math>r>0</math>,

:<math>\begin{align}
\operatorname{Pr}(|X-\alpha|\ge r)\le \begin{cases}
\frac{4\rho^2}{9r^2}&r\ge \sqrt{8/3}\rho \\
\frac{4\rho^2}{3r^2}-\frac{1}{3}&r\le \sqrt{8/3}\rho. \\
\end{cases}
\end{align}</math>

=== Relation to Gauss's inequality ===

Taking <math>\alpha</math> equal to a mode of <math>X</math> yields the first case of [[Gauss's inequality]].

=== Tightness of Bound ===

[[Without loss of generality]], assume <math>\alpha=0</math> and <math>\rho=1</math>.

* If <math>r<1</math>, the left-hand side can equal one, so the bound is useless.

* If <math>r\ge \sqrt{8/3}</math>, the bound is tight when <math>X=0</math> with probability <math>1-\frac{4}{3r^2}</math> and is otherwise distributed uniformly in the interval <math>\left[-\frac{3r}{2},\frac{3r}{2}\right]</math>.

* If <math>1\le r\le \sqrt{8/3}</math>, the bound is tight when <math>X=r</math> with probability <math>\frac{4}{3r^2}-\frac{1}{3}</math> and is otherwise distributed uniformly in the interval <math>\left[-\frac{r}{2},r\right]</math>.

=== Specialization to mean and variance ===

If <math>X</math> has mean <math>\mu</math> and finite, non-zero variance <math>\sigma^2</math>, then taking <math>\alpha=\mu</math> and <math>r=\lambda \sigma</math> gives that for any <math display=inline>\lambda > \sqrt{\frac{8}{3}} = 1.63299...,</math>

:<math>\operatorname{Pr}(\left|X-\mu\right|\geq \lambda\sigma)\leq\frac{4}{9\lambda^2}.</math>

=== Proof Sketch ===

For a relatively [[elementary proof]] see.<ref name="Pukelsheim">[https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/2684253.pdf Pukelsheim, F., 1994. The Three Sigma Rule. ''The American Statistician'', 48(2), pp.88-91]</ref> The rough idea behind the proof is that there are two cases: one where the mode of <math>X</math> is close to <math>\alpha</math> compared to <math>r</math>, in which case we can show <math>\operatorname{Pr}(|X-\alpha|\ge r)\le \frac{4\rho^2}{9r^2}</math>, and one where the mode of <math>X</math> is far from <math>\alpha</math> compared to <math>r</math>, in which case we can show <math>\operatorname{Pr}(|X-\alpha|\ge r)\le \frac{4\rho^2}{3r^2}-\frac{1}{3}</math>. Combining these two cases gives <math>\operatorname{Pr}(|X-\alpha|\ge r)\le \max\left(\frac{4\rho^2}{9r^2},\frac{4\rho^2}{3r^2}-\frac{1}{3}\right).</math> When <math>\frac{r}{\rho}=\sqrt{\frac{8}{3}}</math>, the two cases give the same value.

== Properties ==

The theorem refines [[Chebyshev's inequality]] by including the factor of 4/9, made possible by the condition that the distribution be unimodal.

It is common, in the construction of [[control chart]]s and other statistical heuristics, to set {{math|1=λ = 3}}, corresponding to an upper probability bound of 4/81=&nbsp;0.04938..., and to construct ''3-sigma'' limits to bound ''nearly all'' (i.e. 95%) of the values of a process output. Without unimodality Chebyshev's inequality would give a looser bound of {{math|1= 1/9 = 0.11111...}}.

== One-sided version ==

A version of the Vysochanskij-Petunin inequality for one-sided tail bounds exists. For a unimodal random variable <math>X</math> with mean <math>\mu
</math> and variance <math>\sigma^2
</math>, and <math>r \geq 0</math>, a one-sided Vysochanskij-Petunin inequality derived by Mercadier and Strobel (2021)<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mercadier |first1=Mathieu |last2=Strobel |first2=Frank |date=2021-11-16 |title=A one-sided Vysochanskii-Petunin inequality with financial applications |url=http://pure-oai.bham.ac.uk/ws/files/114841826/OSVP_EJOR_accepted.pdf |journal=European Journal of Operational Research |language=en |volume=295 |issue=1 |pages=374–377 |doi=10.1016/j.ejor.2021.02.041 |issn=0377-2217}}</ref> holds as follows:

:<math>\mathbb{P}(X-\mu\geq r)\leq
			\begin{cases}
				\dfrac{4}{9}\dfrac{\sigma^2}{r^{2}+\sigma^2} & \mbox{for }r^{2}\geq\dfrac{5}{3}\sigma^2,\\
				\dfrac{4}{3}\dfrac{\sigma^2}{r^{2}+\sigma^2}-\dfrac{1}{3} & \mbox{otherwise.}
			\end{cases}
</math>

The above Mercadier-Strobel inequality, as well as the related [[Cantelli's inequality|Cantelli inequality]], can for instance be relevant in the financial area, in the sense of "how bad can losses get".

=== Proof ===

The proof is very similar to that of [[Cantelli's_inequality#Proof|Cantelli's inequality]]. For any <math>u\ge 0</math>,

:<math>\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}(X-\mu\geq r)&=\mathbb{P}((X+u)-\mu\geq r+u)\\
&\le \mathbb{P}(|(X+u)-\mu)|\geq r+u).\\
\end{align}</math>

Then we can apply the Vysochanskij-Petunin inequality. With <math>\rho^2=\mathbb E[((X+u)-\mu)^2]=u^2+\sigma^2</math>, we have:

:<math>
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}(|(X+u)-\mu)|\geq r+u) &\le \begin{cases}
\frac{4}{9} \frac{\rho^2}{(r+u)^2} & r+u\ge \sqrt{8/3}\rho\\
\frac{4}{3} \frac{\rho^2}{(r+u)^2}-\frac{1}{3} & r+u\le \sqrt{8/3}\rho
\end{cases}.
\end{align}
</math>

As in the proof of Cantelli's inequality, it can be shown that the minimum of <math>\frac{\rho^2}{(r+u)^2}</math> over all <math>u\ge 0</math> is achieved at <math>u=\sigma^2/r</math>. Plugging in this value of <math>u</math> and simplifying yields the desired inequality.

==Generalisation==
Dharmadhikari and Joag-Dev generalised the VP inequality to deviations from an arbitrary point and moments of order <math>k</math> other than <math>2</math>
:<math>
\begin{align}
P(|X-\alpha| \geq r) \leq \max \left\{\frac{s \tau_k-r^k}{(s-1) r^k},\left[\frac{k}{k+1}\right]^k \frac{\tau_k}{r^k}\right\} \\
\end{align}
</math>
where
:<math>
\begin{align}
\tau_k=E\left(|X-\alpha|^k\right), s>(k+1),  s(s-k-1)^k=k^k
\end{align}
</math>
The standard form of the inequality can be recovered by setting <math>k = 2</math> which leads to a unique value of <math>s = 4</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dharmadhikari |first1=S. W. |last2=Joag-Dev |first2=K. |year=1986 |title=The Gauss–Tchebyshev inequality for unimodal distributions |journal=Theory of Probability & Its Applications |volume=30 |issue=4 |pages=867–871 |doi=10.1137/1130111 }}</ref>
